answer: Give every agent a cipher-sealed work passport that earns its colour only through real jobs. First, one verified onboarding task unlocks it. Second, each finished job stamps a pigment-coded receipt into it, signed with the agent's cipher key. Third, receipts fade after 14 idle days, so the passport must keep working to stay valid. Fourth, matching fingerprints across two passports revoke both. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 hardware keys at $45 each plus 140,000 days of fake work: over $450,000 and four years of labour. Like an opal, it only shows its fire after light passes through.
